title: Standardisation and inverse normal with unknown parameters

points.text: Finding an unknown mean or standard deviation from given probabilities

bigPicture: Standardising turns any normal variable into Z ~ N(0, 1). Working backwards from a probability to z is how you find an unknown mean or standard deviation.

keyIdeas.answer: z = (x − μ)/σ: how many standard deviations x lies above (+) or below (−) the mean. Z ~ N(0, 1).

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find an unknown μ or σ?
keyIdeas.answer: Use invNorm on N(0, 1) to get z for the given probability (area to the left), then solve (x − μ)/σ = z. With both unknown, write two such equations and solve them simultaneously.

keyTerms.def: number of standard deviations from the mean

workedExamples.title: One unknown
workedExamples.prompt: X ~ N(μ, 3²) and P(X < 20) = 0.8. Find μ.

misconceptions.wrong: Using the probability itself as z
Sign of z for a value below the mean
misconceptions.right: Below the mean z is negative.

practice.prompt: For X ~ N(μ, 5²), the value x = 64 has z-value 2. Find μ.
X ~ N(μ, σ²) with P(X < 30) = 0.1 and P(X > 50) = 0.2. Find μ and σ.
